Fundraising for a cubs uniform - aged 7
Graphic change needed?: Photo of me as a kid
Instructions / notes: I took a tin can and knocked on doors in the neighborhood askng for donations for my cubs uniform. Our family was financially strapped at the time, which was a part of my pitch. Outcome: A kick up the bum, and return all monies to people, and a cubs uniforms!

Graphic change needed?: Photo of me as a 11 year old
Instructions / notes: My Intermediate school ran a plastic freezer and sandwich bag selling campaing to raise money. For 2.5 month I cycled across Hastings, Hawkes Bay, knocking on doors selling them. Final count was I was just shy of selling more than the entire school combined sales. Outcome: I won the scientific calculator.

Booked a band and built a multi level stage with my father for them to perform on. Targeted the 'popular students' at the highschools in our city, with a sales incentive of a free ticket for every 10 sold. Outcome: Party of the year, with 350 teenagers causing abolute mayhem. Despite being a very profitable exercise, permission to repeat it was declined.

At the tender age of 15 I began hairdressing in what I later discovered was the central hub of NZ's most talented hairdressers. Continued the hairdressing journey working at Grace (Wgtn), Cut Above (Auck) and Kaos Hair Control (Auck) until 20 years old, when I realised the income I sought could only be achieved by ownign multiple salons - and managing mulitple hairdressers. Left the profession.

Explored the world of high fashion and modeling, working for Maysie Bestall-Cohen in Auckland. It went hand in hand with hairdressing, though found the scene and values m,isaligned with my own. Decined an offer to move to Australia and work with a new agency Maysie was opening in Sydney.

Purchased 10K worth of DJ equipment and sound gear and began self education and throwing events. 4 years later and countless attempts be repossession agents to take my gear, I paid it off. No longer producing events, last count was over 130.

Began my first legit paid sales role. An early tech business with 4 digit code on the back of phone books that took dialers to adverts from paid advertisers e.g. plumbers, mower repaiers etc. Achieved highest sales in NZ, despite the venture never really getting traction long term.

Spent the entire 1999 year producing the largest private millenium event in NZ. 15,000 people, 2 stages with Pearl Jam's same rig on band stage, 12 x 3 metres stacks of JBL sound gear in dance marquee with 96 intelligent lights and 2 full colour lasers. Sold naming rights to DB for 10 seconds of the laser at midnight for 36K. All NZ lineup including The Exponents, Mark de Clive Lowe, Bongmaster (became Fat Freddy's Drop), The New Loungehead, Matt Drake, Andy Vann, DJ Lemon and many more.

My beautiful daughter Molly was born, on March 2nd 2001. I learned more about myself parenting her, than any other part of my life. She has blossomed into a strong, creative and kind young woman who completed her degree at Toi Whakaari (NZ Drama School) in 2024. Molly finished with a 96% average pass rate and supported herself finacially throughtout the grueling degree. Now living in Berlin with her fantastic partner Thomas, she's having the time of her life with a well earned year off.

Had to get serious, had a family to provide for. Tried to keep DJ'ing, as music and playing it was such a passion. Lasted around 6 months when I realised playing out late and sleeping in was causing me to miss my daughter too much. Stopped performing in public though never stoppped following cutting edge jazz infused electronic body music (music made for dancing!) The rest of my journey can be found in my CV (add link?)
